transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-08 15:00 PT — Duration ~52m — Attendees: Alex (Redwood CSM), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Redwood Support) — Tom (CTO), Maya (Head of AI), Sarah (SecOps), Vikram (Platform)

Summary: quick alignment call; this is kickoff for activation + technical intake for Orion's claims automation pilot.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes, so we'll run through a quick agenda — intro, success metrics, network/security, pilot plan, next steps. any additions?
[00:12] Tom (Orion): no that's good, alex, thanks. i'm mostly on to make sure we can meet the latency and compliance constraints for the claims flow.
[00:21] Maya (Orion): and from ML side we want to validate hallucination rates on our prompts — if redwood can help with eval hooks that'd be great.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood): yeah totally, we have hooks in the console for prompt sets and eval monitoring; we'll show that in the POC. quick question — are you planning hosted API or dedicated / private?
[00:42] Vikram (Orion): we prefer dedicated capacity initially to keep consistent throughput and the option to VPC peer into our environment. security wants private control plane but we'll see.
[00:50] Sarah (Orion): yep, SOC2 is required and we need audit logs forwarded. also SAML SSO for access.
[00:58] Alex (Redwood): good, that's in line with what we typically do for enterprise customers — we can support dedicated GPU pools and we offer a private deployment option if you need an on-prem box. for pilot, dedicated reserved capacity with VPC peering is common.
[01:12] Tom: what's the timeline to get a pilot up and running? we have a product sprint end of july and would like to run a small trial in august.
[01:20] Priya: realistically, if we get your prompt sets and expected TPS numbers this week, we can provision a pilot environment in about 1–2 weeks — so mid-july for infra, early august testing.
[01:34] Maya: ok that aligns. for throughput, we're expecting bursts up to 70 requests per minute for claims triage, average seq length maybe 400 tokens.
[01:45] Priya: that's helpful — sequence length and burst patterns drive kernel choices and batching. our runtime will suggest config for batching windows to hit latency SLOs.
[01:55] Daniel (Redwood): one note on cost — dedicated capacity pricing is commit-based, we'll show different slot sizes in the quote. rough estimates depend on batch configurations and quantization level.
[02:07] Tom: can you send an initial cost example for our expected workload? we need to compare to Anthropic pricing and our internal self-host estimates.
[02:15] Alex: yes we'll include a cost run-down in the follow-up.

[02:30] Topic: Network & Security
[02:33] Priya: Vikram, can you say what your network constraints are? CIDR ranges, do you allow VPC peering, any egress filtering?
[02:42] Vikram: we can do VPC peering to a dedicated sub-net, we'll share our CIDR list. egress is restricted, but we allow outbound to vendor IPs after review. encryption-at-rest is mandatory; we use AWS KMS and want to bring our own keys.
[02:58] Sarah: also need proof of SOC2, how long is the retention on logs, can we ship audit logs to our SIEM?
[03:06] Alex: yes SOC2 report can be shared under NDA, we can forward audit log delivery options — syslog forwarding to your SIEM or S3 buckets with restricted access. KMS BYOK is supported; we also support HSM integrations for private deployments.
[03:22] Maya: in terms of data residency — claims data must remain in EU region for a subset of customers. can you pin model endpoints to specific regions?
[03:31] Priya: region pinning is supported; we can deploy dedicated pools in eu-west or us-west depending on your needs.

[03:45] Tom: any concerns about KV cache leaking PII between requests? we plan to use prefix caching for session continuity.
[03:53] Priya: our runtime isolates KV caches per-tenant, and we can configure TTLs and purge on demand. still, any PII handling should be filtered client-side when possible.

[04:07] Topic: Pilot scope and success metrics
[04:10] Alex: let's define success — what does a successful pilot look like in two weeks?
[04:15] Maya: functional accuracy: <5% critical hallucinations on the claims dataset;
[04:20] Tom: latency: p95 under 450ms for single-turn generation in the pilot;
[04:26] Vikram: reliability: 99.5% availability during business hours;
[04:31] Sarah: security: SOC2 evidence and KMS BYOK confirmed.
[04:35] Priya: ok we'll instrument metrics in the console — token breakdown, latency heatmaps, error rates. we'll also run baseline evals against your prompt sets.

[04:50] Maya: one more machine learning question — we'd like the ability to pin a specific model version and fall back to a smaller quantized variant if capacity spikes. is that supported?
[04:59] Priya: yes, model pinning and automatic fallback policies exist. we can configure a routing policy: prefer model A, fallback to model B (quantized) after X% latency or if capacity constrained.

[05:12] Topic: Integration details and sample flow
[05:15] Priya: typical integration is: you call Redwood SDK with the conversation and session metadata, we return tokens and a conversation ID. can you walk through your orchestrator?
[05:24] Vikram: we have a microservice that handles claim intake, calls the model for triage, then persists outputs in our claims DB. we want deterministic outputs for auditability so we plan to log prompts and model responses to immutable storage.
[05:35] Alex: note on determinism — sampling temperature affects variability; for audit picks we recommend lower temp or deterministic decoding. also we can attach model metadata and model version to every response in the headers.
[05:48] Tom: is there a retention policy for the logs you keep? we want to control what Redwood retains vs what we ingest into our own storage.
[05:55] Daniel: retention on the Redwood side is configurable per-customer — we can set short-lived retention for pilot and provide export hooks.

[06:05] Topic: Compliance doc requests
[06:08] Sarah: please share: SOC2 report, penetration test summary, data processing addendum, and SAML integration guide.
[06:14] Alex: will do. we'll upload the docs to the secure share and flag any items requiring NDA.

[06:20] Maya: can Redwood provide baseline eval scripts we can run with our dataset? for measuring hallucination and fidelity
[06:26] Priya: yes we have eval harnesses — prompt set runner, BLEU-like metrics, hallucination detection heuristics. we'll share the repo and example queries.

[06:36] Topic: Rollout strategy and risk mitigation
[06:39] Alex: for rollout we recommend canary -> ramp -> full. for canary, route a small % to Redwood and monitor. in outages we can fallback to a smaller model or queue requests.
[06:50] Tom: how fast is failover between variants?
[06:53] Priya: instant at the routing layer — switch is config-only and we can trigger programmatic rollbacks. stateful KV caches may warm-up; we'll note that for latency considerations.

[07:05] Vikram: about observability — we need token-level billing breakdowns so we can reconcile spend to request types.
[07:12] Daniel: console exposes token and cost per route; we can also provide CSV exports and webhook alerts on spend thresholds.

[07:22] Maya: any special considerations for training / fine-tuning? we might want a small RLHF run later.
[07:28] Priya: fine-tuning is an add-on; for production inference you can host a fine-tuned model and Redwood can serve it, but we'd need to vet size and quantization strategy. we can discuss in a follow-up.

[07:40] Quick Q&A / interruptions and clarifications
[07:42] Sarah: do you support SAML SCIM for user provisioning?
[07:45] Alex: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported for enterprise accounts.
[07:49] Tom: curious about cold start token penalties with long sequences?
[07:53] Priya: cold start mostly affects initial warm-up for KV cache; continuous batching mitigates per-token overhead. for long sequences we select kernels optimized for your seq length distribution.

[08:05] Closing and recap
[08:07] Alex: ok to recap — action items: alex will share runbook + SOC2, priya will spin up pilot infra, orion will send prompts and CIDRs, sarah will confirm KMS choice, tom will send success metrics. three follow-ups: onboarding docs by fri 7/10, technical deep dive week of 7/13, pilot infra by 7/15.
[08:25] Tom: that works. thanks team.
[08:28] Maya: thanks everyone.
[08:30] Daniel: i'll follow up in the thread with the SOC2 link and the onboarding checklist.

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and minor word swaps (e.g., k v cache sometimes transcribed as "K-V" or "key V cache"), filler words present.

References shared: onboarding_runbook.pdf (link shared in chat), SOC2-summary.pdf (link pending NDA), pilot-config-template.csv

End of meeting.
